A Nuevo Laredo high school student just earned a spot on a national stage — with a paint formula that could help both sides of the border beat the heat. José Miguel Montes Camacho, an evening-shift student at the Preparatoria Municipal de Nuevo Laredo Elena Poniatowska, has qualified for ExpoCiencias Nacional 2026 Nuevo León, one of Mexico's top youth science competitions.

According to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, Montes Camacho won his ticket at the state-level Certamen Estatal de Creatividad e Innovación Tecnológica Expo Ciencias Tamaulipas 2026 with a project called “Eco Hidro, Pintura ecológica” — a non-toxic, biodegradable paint made from natural elements that repels water and humidity and helps regulate indoor temperatures in both heat and cold.

Paint that fights the border heat

In a border city where summers are brutal and cooling costs eat family budgets, a paint that reflects heat and resists moisture isn't just a school project — it's a practical idea with real-world legs. The formula's ingredients are natural and non-toxic, which means it's safer for the students and families who would use it than conventional coatings.

Montes Camacho will present Eco Hidro at ExpoCiencias Nacional 2026 in Monterrey, Nuevo León, from November 11 to 14 — competing against young innovators from across the country.

A school that keeps producing winners

School director Nidia Benavides Casso praised Montes Camacho's ingenuity, effort and dedication, as well as that of his advisor, teacher Ricardo Escobedo Rodríguez. She described the school as a breeding ground for student projects, saying students are digging deeper into science and technology and coming up with more ideas to invent or improve products.

The track record backs her up: this year, students from the same preparatory school took first places in mathematics, physics, chemistry and administration at a basic-sciences contest organized by the Instituto Tecnológico de Nuevo Laredo.

When a public evening-shift high school in Nuevo Laredo keeps churning out state champions in math, science and innovation, that's not luck — that's a pipeline. José Miguel Montes Camacho carries that pipeline's latest entry to Monterrey in November. Both Laredos should be rooting for him.
